## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

DataLayerMessageChannel — core-sync/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/sync/transport/MessageChannel.kt

## Trigger

`send` is already called from `WearableProfileSyncTransport.send`, `WearableRecordedRaceTransport.send` and `WearableRecordedRaceAckTransport.send` whenever a profile, a recorded race or an acknowledgement is sent — observed. The scope tear-down that cancels the coroutine mid-send comes from outside `:core-sync` (the caller's own scope) and is not itself a call to observe.

## Today

`DataLayerMessageChannel.send` (MessageChannel.kt) wraps `nodeClient.connectedNodes.await()` and `messageClient.sendMessage(...).await()` in `try { … } catch (other: Exception) { false }`. `WearableProfileSyncTransport.send`, `WearableRecordedRaceTransport.send` and `WearableRecordedRaceAckTransport.send` each wrap their call to `channel.send(...)` in the same `try { … } catch (other: Exception) { false }` shape. `CancellationException` is a subtype of `Exception`, so a scope cancelled while any of these four `await()`/`send()` calls is suspended is caught and reported as `false` (a delivery failure) instead of being rethrown to unwind the coroutine, in all four places. `HrHistoryReaderImpl.bpmValuesOverLast12Months` (app-phone/src/main/java/com/mgilli/hyroxtracker/health/HrHistoryReaderImpl.kt) already shows the correct shape: `catch (e: CancellationException) { throw e }` placed before `catch (e: Exception) { emptyList() }`.

## Expected

Each of the four `send` implementations catches `CancellationException` first and rethrows it, before its existing `catch (other: Exception) { false }`, the way `HrHistoryReaderImpl` does. This is one mechanical fix repeated at four independent sites — the three transports each hold their own `try/catch` around `channel.send(...)`, out of `DataLayerMessageChannel`'s reach, so rethrowing cancellation in `DataLayerMessageChannel` alone is not enough: `WearableProfileSyncTransport.send`, `WearableRecordedRaceTransport.send` and `WearableRecordedRaceAckTransport.send` each still catch `Exception` around the call to `channel.send(...)` and would swallow a `CancellationException` re-thrown from below unless each of their own catch blocks is fixed too. The KDoc on `MessageChannel.send` ("False on any delivery failure — never throws") also needs updating to reflect that cancellation is no longer treated as a delivery failure.
